transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-03-12
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Evan Brooks (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Astra - Head of SecOps), Marco Ruiz (Astra - Eng Lead), Claire Nguyen (Astra - PM)

Summary: Quick demo of data-retention controls in Redwood Console and API. Showed redaction rules, request storage toggles, and purge workflow. Discussed tradeoffs for storing requests for quality and observability vs privacy/regs.

[00:00:05] Evan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros — I'm Evan, AE on the account, and Maya's our SE who will walk through the Console demo.
[00:00:18] Priya: Hi, thanks. Priya here — SecOps. We'll be mainly focused on retention windows and proof of deletion.
[00:00:25] Marco: Marco, eng lead. Curious about API flags and how to do this programmatically.
[00:00:30] Claire: Claire, product. I want to understand what we can still do on Optimize if we don't store requests.
[00:00:40] Maya: Great. Quick agenda: Console walkthrough for Data Controls, show API payload toggles like store_requests=false, demo redaction rule editor, then Q&A.
[00:00:55] Evan: Also will touch briefly on hosted vs private differences for audit logs and KMS.

[00:01:30] Maya: (screen share) So in Console -> Settings -> Data Controls — you'll see toggles at org and route level. Top-level toggle is "Request storage" with choices: store full, store minimal (metadata only), and do not store. You can also set default retention_days.
[00:01:57] Marco: Is "do not store" absolute? Like, will any logs still keep snippets for debugging?
[00:02:10] Maya: Good question. On hosted, "do not store" will prevent request/response payloads from being written to long-term storage; ephemeral tracing for debugging (e.g., 5 minute window) may still exist in ephemeral logs for crash analysis, but not searchable transcripts. For Private deployments you can configure retention to zero and have audit logs forwarded to your SIEM, per your KMS/HSM settings.
[00:02:40] Priya: When you say ephemeral, can you show where that's set? We need proof that data leaves within X minutes.
[00:02:48] Maya: Sure — under Advanced -> Traces. There's an ephemeral_trace_ttl setting; it's default 10 minutes for hosted but we can reduce. I'll show the API as well.

[00:03:30] [Maya navigates]
[00:03:45] Maya: Here's the redaction rules editor. Two modes: regex-based and ML-PII. Regex rules apply in order and you can preview against examples. ML-PII is model-driven detection for names, emails, CC numbers etc. You can choose to redact or mask — redaction replaces token sequences with [REDACTED].
[00:04:05] Priya: How are regex rules applied? Is it before or after tokenization?
[00:04:12] Maya: Before tokenization — it's run on the raw string; then ML-PII runs as a second pass. Note: ML-PII may have false positives, you can set confidence thresholds.
[00:04:30] Marco: And those redaction rules are org-wide? Or per-route?
[00:04:36] Maya: Both — default org rules plus route-level overrides. So you can have stricter rules for routes hitting sensitive workflows.

[00:05:00] Evan: API example — you can pass store_requests=false in the request header or payload. We showed a quick curl earlier:
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer ..." -d '{"input":"...","store_requests":false}'
[00:05:30] Claire: If we set store_requests=false, do we lose telemetry that's used by Optimize?
[00:05:40] Maya: By default, yes — Optimize uses sample payloads to surface regression alerts. But we provide an anonymized sampling mode where we can hash tokens and still send metadata like latency and token counts. That lets Optimize recommend batching/quantization without seeing raw PII.
[00:06:05] Priya: Do you have an example of the anonymization?
[00:06:10] Maya: (switches tab) Here's an anonymization preview — email -> <hash:...>, long text -> truncated to first 200 chars + hash. We can also strip entire fields via the API.

[00:06:40] Marco: Ok, about deletion requests — how does purge work? If we ask to delete all calls for a user, how fast is that and what guarantees?
[00:06:50] Maya: On hosted, we have a documented deletion pipeline: a request goes to the purge queue, objects flagged for deletion are removed from S3-like store and indexes updated. Typical completion for a standard org is <24 hours, we provide a purge id you can track. For Private, you control the retention and can run immediate deletes locally.
[00:07:15] Priya: Can we get a signed attestation that data was deleted?
[00:07:20] Evan: We can provide an audit log of the purge operation IDs, timestamps, and the storage objects removed. For compliance, we can coordinate with your legal to produce attestations but that's a separate process.

[00:07:45] [00:07:50] Marco: How granular is the retention? Per-org, per-model, per-route?
[00:07:55] Maya: You can set retention at org level, then override per-route or per-model. There's also tag-based rules — if you label a route as "sensitive" retention can be shorter.

[00:08:30] Priya: About audit logs — where are they stored? Can we forward them to Splunk?
[00:08:36] Maya: Yes, we support forwarding audit logs to external sinks: Splunk, Datadog, S3, or your SIEM via secure webhook or syslog. We support envelope encryption with your KMS key (bring-your-own-key) for Private and select Hosted tiers.
[00:08:55] Priya: Is the envelope encryption audited?
[00:08:58] Maya: We log KMS key usage in the audit logs — key IDs and usage timestamps; the actual plaintext never leaves the HSM.

[00:09:20] Claire: A product question — if we don't store requests, how do we do prompt quality reviews later?
[00:09:28] Evan: Options: 1) sampling: store e.g., 0.1% of requests for manual review, 2) anonymize/hash tokens and store, 3) store-derived metrics and embeddings for quality evals. Optimize can run evals without raw text by using embeddings and metrics.

[00:10:00] [Maya shows API console]
[00:10:12] Maya: Programmatically there's a request header x-redwood-store: false or payload key store_requests=false. For logs we emit meta attributes: request_id, route_id, user_id (optional hashed). These meta fields remain even if store_requests=false.
[00:10:40] Marco: Are there any performance impacts to redaction or ML-PII in the request path?
[00:10:46] Maya: Minimal — regex redaction is sub-ms in our pipeline. ML-PII uses a lightweight detector; on average adds ~5-15ms per request depending on text length. We have async redaction for very large payloads if you prefer no impact on latency.

[00:11:20] Priya: For SOC 2 we need retention tables. Can you send a matrix of where data lives and default retention windows?
[00:11:26] Evan: Yes — that's one of the action items. We'll include the default retention per data type (requests, logs, traces, audit events) and hosted vs private differences.

[00:11:45] Marco: Demo a purge now? I want to see a purge id come back.
[00:11:50] Maya: I can run a sandbox purge on the demo dataset. Running curl now...
[00:12:20] [murmur]
[00:12:25] Maya: Okay purge queued — purge_id: purge-20250312-xyz. Status: queued. I'll show subsequent status update where it moves to in_progress then completed.
[00:12:40] Priya: That ID is good, we can track. Do you expose which storage objects were removed or only counts?
[00:12:47] Maya: We provide both: list of object ids and counts per object type. For security/ops reasons the low-level object path is hashed in the response.

[00:13:10] Claire: One more on search — if we redact, do we still surface search results?
[00:13:15] Maya: We index metadata and redacted tokens depending on rule settings. There's an option "index_after_redaction"— if set false, the original tokens won't be searchable, only metadata will.

[00:13:45] Evan: I'll highlight hosted vs private briefly: in Private you get full control: you decide retention, you host audit logs; in hosted we offer BYOK and enterprise controls but some controls are limited by isolation model.
[00:14:00] Priya: For private deployments, we need a statement how Key rotation is audited.
[00:14:05] Maya: We log key rotations. We can provide a Key Rotation Policy doc.

[00:14:35] [Interruption - background noise]
[00:14:50] Marco: Sorry noise — quick Q on compliance — does Redwood support data residency in EU only?
[00:14:56] Evan: Yes, we have regions with EU-only storage for hosted customers; you can pin to eu-west-1 region. Private obviously runs in your VPC/region.

[00:15:25] Priya: Ok appreciate that. Can we customize redaction rules via API? We have a long list of internal IDs to drop.
[00:15:32] Maya: Yes — there's an API to upload regex rules or a ruleset file. You can also version rules and roll back.

[00:16:00] [Maya demos rule upload]
[00:16:30] Maya: Example rule: {"pattern":"(?i)SSN[:\\s]*\\\\d{3}-\\\\d{2}-\\\\d{4}", "action":"redact"}. In the console you can preview against recent logs.
[00:16:55] Priya: Perfect. On attestations — how quickly can you generate an export for legal showing deletion?
[00:17:02] Evan: The purge audit is available immediately and we can produce a signed statement within a week, depending on the legal scope. We'll coordinate offline.

[00:17:40] Claire: Regarding Optimize — if we use anonymized samples will Optimize still suggest batching tweaks?
[00:17:48] Maya: Yes, Optimize mostly uses token counts and latency traces. Anonymized payloads preserve length distribution so recommendations remain high quality.

[00:18:10] [Customer asks about costs]
[00:18:15] Marco: Is there an extra cost for storing data longer or for encryption with BYOK?
[00:18:22] Evan: BYOK itself is not charged, but long-term cold storage and additional retention beyond default may incur a storage fee. We'll put cost tiers in the doc we send.

[00:18:45] Priya: Any regulatory gaps you see that we should be worried about (GDPR, CCPA)?
[00:18:52] Evan: None fundamental — Redwood's hosted product supports compliance controls, but you must scope data flows with your legal to confirm. For strict GDPR requirements, private deployment or EU-only hosting is the conservative path.

[00:19:20] Maya: Quick note on logs: audit events (login, key use, config changes) are retained separately from request payloads and have their own retention policy.

[00:19:45] Marco: Can we pull logs programmatically for retention review?
[00:19:50] Maya: Yes there's an audit logs API that returns JSON events, and you can request bulk exports.

[00:20:10] [Longer demo of Console redaction previews]
[00:24:00] [00:24:12] Priya: I'm worried about ML-PII false negatives. How do you measure detection accuracy?
[00:24:20] Maya: We have evaluation sets and thresholds; we expose detection confidence per span. You can tune threshold to trade recall vs precision. We'll share our eval metrics in the security pack.

[00:25:30] Marco: For infra — does redaction run on GPU or CPU? Concerned about cost & latency.
[00:25:36] Maya: Regex runs on CPU. ML-PII runs on a small CPU-optimized model; no GPU required. Latency impact is relatively low.

[00:26:10] Evan: Ok, let's recap and call out next steps.
[00:26:20] Evan: Action items we captured: Evan to send SOC2 and retention matrix; Maya to enable sandbox with toggles and run purge demo and provide purge_id logs; Priya to share legal retention windows. We'll schedule the deeper technical session.

[00:26:40] Priya: Sounds good. One ask: show us the exact API response when store_requests=false — are we still returning request_id?
[00:26:48] Maya: Yes, we return request_id and low-level metadata so you can reconcile events without payload. Example response: {"request_id":"req-12345","status":"processed","stored":false}.
[00:27:10] [Some crosstalk about scheduling]
[00:28:00] Marco: Can we get a sandbox where we test key rotation?
[00:28:05] Evan: Yes we'll do that.

[00:28:40] Claire: Thanks — this clarified a lot. For product we'll review the anonymization examples.

[00:29:00] Evan: Any final questions?
[00:29:06] Priya: One last — how do you handle third-party integrations that may log payloads, like support tickets?
[00:29:12] Maya: We have integration settings; for e.g., if you forward transcripts to Zendesk you can apply redaction rules prior to the forward. There's a pipeline rule to strip or mask fields before outbound sink.

[00:29:40] Marco: Ok good.
[00:29:50] Evan: Great, we'll follow up with the docs and sandbox. Thanks everyone.
[00:29:58] Meeting ended.

Notes on transcription quality: some technical terms may be slightly off (e.g., "KV cache" transcribed as "K V cash" in parts). There are filler words and occasional overlapped speech.
